text:
Roope Hintz is the engine nobody talks about on a Dallas team that has won eight of its last ten. He has 21 points in 23 games at about 16.5 minutes a night, and with him on the ice at five on five the Stars have taken 53% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, four points better than without him.

His last ten games brought 11 points against about 8 expected, with the Stars scoring a bit more than their chances deserve when he's out there. He's also shooting 19% against a league norm of 13.5, so a little of this is hot. But the ceiling is real: our range for his scoring rate runs from 2.4 to 3.3 points per 60, well above the league's 2.1.

Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among forwards in wins above replacement last season, and it was his defense that stood out, opponents' chances shrinking with him on at a 99th percentile rate. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 55% of his shots came off the rush. Watch the transition game; that's where he hurts teams.
